subject: Plot death rates by age for successive decades

messages.author: a1fe38ed8c0012da
messages.subject: Plot death rates by age for successive decades
parts:
I wanted to plot tuberculosis mortality by successive decades for various age categories. The data was abstracted from this webpage:

http://aje.oxfordjournals.org.proxy.kib.ki.se/content/141/1/4.long



The death numbers for each decade are given per 100000 and I wish to plot age on x axis and the death rates on y axis 

structure(list(age = c("0-4", "5-9", "10-19", "20-29", "30-39", 
"40-49", "50-59", "60-69", "70+"), `1880` = c(760L, 43L, 126L, 
444L, 378L, 364L, 366L, 475L, 672L), `1890` = c(578L, 49L, 115L, 
361L, 368L, 336L, 325L, 346L, 396L), `1900` = c(309L, 31L, 90L, 
288L, 296L, 253L, 267L, 304L, 343L), `1910` = c(209L, 21L, 63L, 
207L, 253L, 253L, 252L, 246L, 163L), `1920` = c(108L, 24L, 49L, 
149L, 164L, 175L, 171L, 172L, 127L), `1930` = c(41L, 11L, 21L, 
81L, 115L, 118L, 127L, 95L, 95L)), datalabel = "", time.stamp = "25 Jun 2015 17:15", .Names = c("age", 
"1880", "1890", "1900", "1910", "1920", "1930"), formats = c("%9s", 
"%8.0g", "%8.0g", "%8.0g", "%8.0g", "%8.0g", "%8.0g"), types = c(5L, 
252L, 252L, 252L, 252L, 252L, 252L), val.labels = c("", "", "", 
"", "", "", ""), var.labels = c("", "", "", "", "", "", ""), row.names = c("1", 
"2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9"), version = 12L, class = "data.frame")


Thanks

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Plot death rates by age for successive decades
parts:
You're probably wanting something like this, but it's a rainbow dynamite plot: 

library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

df <- structure(list(age = c("0-4", "5-9", "10-19", "20-29", "30-39",

"40-49", "50-59", "60-69", "70+"), `1880` = c(760L, 43L, 126L, 
444L, 378L, 364L, 366L, 475L, 672L), `1890` = c(578L, 49L, 115L, 
361L, 368L, 336L, 325L, 346L, 396L), `1900` = c(309L, 31L, 90L, 
288L, 296L, 253L, 267L, 304L, 343L), `1910` = c(209L, 21L, 63L, 
207L, 253L, 253L, 252L, 246L, 163L), `1920` = c(108L, 24L, 49L, 
149L, 164L, 175L, 171L, 172L, 127L), `1930` = c(41L, 11L, 21L, 
81L, 115L, 118L, 127L, 95L, 95L)), datalabel = "", time.stamp = "25 Jun 2015 17:15", .Names = c("age", 
"1880", "1890", "1900", "1910", "1920", "1930"), formats = c("%9s", 
"%8.0g", "%8.0g", "%8.0g", "%8.0g", "%8.0g", "%8.0g"), types = c(5L, 
252L, 252L, 252L, 252L, 252L, 252L), val.labels = c("", "", "", 
"", "", "", ""), var.labels = c("", "", "", "", "", "", ""), row.names = c("1", 
"2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8", "9"), version = 12L, class = "data.frame")

df %>% 
gather(. , year, deaths, -age) %>%
ggplot(., aes(x=age, y = deaths, fill = year)) + geom_bar(stat="identity", position="dodge")


This might be slightly better:
df %>% 
gather(. , year, deaths, -age) %>%
ggplot(., aes(x=age, y = deaths)) +
geom_point() +
facet_wrap("year", nrow=1) +
theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=90, hjust=1, vjust=0.5))

Just as interesting is to facet by age. The trends are more clear, as are aberrations. 
df %>% 
gather(. , year, deaths, -age) %>%
ggplot(., aes(x=year, y = deaths)) +
geom_point() +
facet_wrap("age", nrow=1) +
theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=90, hjust=1, vjust=0.5))

parts:
Extracting the most important lesson from Brandon's code:

In ggplot you almost always want to work with *long* data (one
observation per row), not *wide* data (your original data frame, with
one column per decade). The solution is to reshape it -- Brandon's
code uses `gather` from the `tidyr` package. Once this step is done,
plotting is straightforward.

Ben

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Plot death rates by age for successive decades
parts: Something like this?

df %>% 
gather(. , year, deaths, -age) %>%

mutate(age = factor(age, levels = c("0-4", "5-9", "10-19", "20-29", "30-39", 
"40-49", "50-59", "60-69", "70+"))) %>%
ggplot(., aes(x=age, y = deaths, colour = year, group=year)) +
geom_line()

If you want the scale on the x-axis to actually be numeric rather than categorical, you'll need to make some decisions on how to treat the ranges of ages.

parts:
Dear Brandon,

I could not run the script as R repeatedly crushed. Have you manged to run it on your pc?

Thanks for your help

On Thursday, June 25, 2015 at 11:33:47 PM UTC+2, Brandon Hurr wrote:
Something like this?

df %>% 
gather(. , year, deaths, -age) %>%
mutate(age = factor(age, levels = c("0-4", "5-9", "10-19", "20-29", "30-39", 
"40-49", "50-59", "60-69", "70+"))) %>%
ggplot(., aes(x=age, y = deaths, colour = year, group=year)) +
geom_line()

If you want the scale on the x-axis to actually be numeric rather than categorical, you'll need to make some decisions on how to treat the ranges of ages. 

On Thu, Jun 25, 2015 at 2:12 PM, Enzo Pacelli <wadd...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Brandon,

https://drive.google.com/file/d/0BwzmHP4sr2DdVXBISmloanZlbU0/view?usp=sharing



Many thanks



On Thursday, June 25, 2015 at 7:15:10 PM UTC+2, Ben wrote:
Extracting the most important lesson from Brandon's code:

In ggplot you almost always want to work with *long* data (one
observation per row), not *wide* data (your original data frame, with
one column per decade). The solution is to reshape it -- Brandon's
code uses `gather` from the `tidyr` package. Once this step is done,
plotting is straightforward.

Ben
